The gate checks that the WORDS `scale` and `filter`/`blur` appear inside the object literal. It never checks that either one ANIMATES. So the exact fade it was built to refuse, rewritten with a non-animating `scale: 1` and `filter: "blur(0px)"` on both `initial` and `animate`, renders pixel-identical to the blocked payload and passes silently. That is a premise defect, not a regex gap: the deny message states the law as "opacity 0 -> 1 | scale 0.96 -> 1 | filter blur(8px) -> blur(0)", and the only value the code ever inspects is `opacity: 0`.

Seven more, each reproduced with hook-probe and a control pair:

1. ACCIDENTAL DISARM, one word. `has_scale = "scale" in body` and `has_blur = ("blur" in body) or ("filter" in body)` are bare substring tests over the whole object body. `initial={{ opacity: 0, filter: "grayscale(1)" }}` satisfies BOTH (grayscale contains "scale", the key is "filter") and passes. So does `initial={{ opacity: 0, scale: 0.96, height: filterPanelHeight }}` with no blur anywhere — and "filter" is this product's core search vocabulary, so an identifier containing it in a motion object is ordinary, not adversarial.

2. THE STAND-DOWN IS THE GATE'S OWN ERROR TEXT. The deny message ends with "Legitimate fade (backdrop/scrim, colour cross-fade)? add `motion-ok: <reason>`." phantom-column-gate.py.defect:
Two independent false-negative classes, both reproduced, both covering the exact incident this gate was built for (bookings.consumed_at in the one-click confirm route).

DEFECT 1 (failure shape 4, the proxy answering a different question). The gate reads only the ADDED text and requires BOTH `.from(` and `.select(` to be inside it (`if ".select(" not in content or ".from(" not in content: allow()`). The ordinary way a column gets added to an existing query is a surgical Edit of the select line alone, which carries `.select(` and no `.from(`. That edit shape is not an edge case here, it is what the project CLAUDE.md orders: "Never rewrite a whole file , change only the lines that cause the reported bug." So the gate is blind in precisely the shape its own house rules mandate. Reproduced on Edit (new_string) and on MultiEdit (edits[]). It is not a tool-registration problem: the same Edit blocks the moment the new_string happens to also contain the `.from(`, so what the gate is really measuring is "did this one hunk happen to include the chain head", used as a proxy for "does this query select a phantom column".

DEFECT 2 (failure shape 2, the same violation in the other spelling the codebase really uses). The round-2 negative lookahead `(?!\.(?:from|update|insert|upsert|delete)\()` was added to stop cross-attribution, and it also silently deletes coverage of every write-then-return chain: `.from(t).insert({...}).select(...)`, `.update({...}).select(...)`, `.upsert({...}).select(...)`, `.delete().select(...)`. All four pass. That is the canonical Supabase "write and return the row" idiom, and it is the exact spelling the missing replay-protection fix would arrive in (`.from("bookings").update({ status }).eq("id", id).select("id, status, consumed_at")`), since consumed_at is set and read in the same statement. Discriminator: deleting only the `.insert({ salon_id })` from that payload makes the identical select BLOCK.

DEFECT 3 (same family as 2, smaller). The 200-char window between `.from(` and `.select(` is exceeded by three ordinary comment lines (measured: 227 chars), and the phantom passes. One comment line, same query, blocks.

DEFECT 4. `.select(BOOKING_COLS)` with the column list in a const passes: the regex demands a quote immediately after `.select(`.

DEFECT 5 (failure shape 5, wrongly refusing correct code). Cross-attribution is only fixed against chains that restart with one of those five verbs. A `.select()` reached through a builder VARIABLE does not restart with any of them, so correct code is refused: `await supabase.from("bookings").eq("id", id).single();` followed by `const { data } = await profilesQuery.select("id, full_name");` is BLOCKED as `bookings.full_name`. I could not show how often that shape occurs in this repo (see the sweep note), so this is a reproduced mechanism, not a measured false-positive count.

DEFECT 6 (sharper form of the escape-hatch note the first agent left). Because ESCAPE is tested against the JOINED MultiEdit content, one legitimate `phantom-ok:` in edit #1 disarms every other edit in the same batch: a batch whose first edit says `// phantom-ok: staff_id landed in the 08-18 migration` and whose second edit selects `consumed_at` passes silently.

SCOPE NOTE, not counted as a defect: the gate reads select lists only, so writing a phantom column in an `.update({ consumed_at: ... })` or `.insert({...})` payload is outside its stated scope entirely, and that is half of the consumed_at fix.
